{{nihongo|'''Mefu Shrine'''|売布神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}, {{ill|Matsue|Q207321|qid=Q207321}}. It is a Shikinaisha, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was designated as a prefectural shrine. It is the sixth site of the {{ill|Izumo Shinbutsu Pilgrimage|Q11395860|qid=Q11395860}}. {{nihongo|'''Mefu Shrine'''|売布神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The principal deity is {{ill|Hayakitsuhiko and Hayakitsuhime|Q11326733|qid=Q11326733|lt=Hayakitsuhime-no-Kami}}, with {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|lt=Isotakeru-no-Kami|Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|Q10935047|qid=Q10935047|lt=Ooyatsuhime-no-Mikoto and Tsumatsuhime-no-Mikoto}} enshrined together as associate deities.

== History ==
It appears in the '{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}' as “Mefu no Yashiro” (賣布社), and in the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' as “Mefu Jinja” (賣布神社). It is said that the shrine was originally located on the western shore of the Irie of Ōi ({{ill|Lake Shinji|Q1151248|qid=Q1151248}}). Due to tidal currents and changes in topography, it was relocated eastward multiple times, and around the {{ill|13th century|Q7049|qid=Q7049}} it came to be enshrined at its present location. There was also a period when it was known as Shirakata Daimyōjin or Hashihime Daimyōjin.

== Subsidiary shrines within the precincts ==
* Wadatatsumi Shrine
* Kotohira Shrine
* Funadama Shrine
* Ebisu Shrine
* Dōsojin Shrine
* Shirakata Tojin Arakami
* Jōkō Shrine
* Ōmatsu Arakami

== Festivals ==
* January 8: Shiokai-sai
* July 12: Funamiyuki Shinto rite
* October 9: Takibi Shinto rite
* October 10: {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}}, Gokyō-sai (Suzuki Festival)

== Surroundings ==
Located in the urban area of Matsue City. The {{ill|Ōhashi River|Q11436587|qid=Q11436587}} flows to the north of the shrine, and the Matsue Shin-Ōhashi Bridge connects it to the northern bank.

== Access ==
* Approximately 500 meters northwest from {{ill|Matsue Station|Q1058652|qid=Q1058652}} on {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125}} (JR West).
